 Inflation triggers another South Dakota minimum wage increase 
 State's hourly minimum for non-tipped workers will climb to $12.30 in 2027 under a formula tied to the Consumer Price Index 
 The Dakota Scout Nov 17, 2026 
 In partnership with 
 Photo by Kamil on Unsplash 
 South Dakota's minimum-wage workers are getting another raise in the new year. 
 The South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation announced Tuesday that the state's minimum wage for non-tipped employees will increase to $12.30 an hour beginning Jan. 1, 2027.

 That's a 45-cent increase from the current $11.85 hourly minimum wage, which took effect Jan. 1, 2026. 
 The annual adjustment is tied to inflation and calculated using changes in the Consumer Price Index published by the U.S. Department of Labor. South Dakota has used the automatic annual increase since 2016, following legislation adopted by state lawmakers in 2015. 
 The minimum wage for tipped employees will increase to $6.15 an hour on Jan. 1, 2027, half the rate required for non-tipped workers. 
 Under state law, employers may pay tipped employees less than the standard minimum wage, but their combined hourly wages and tips must equal at least the full minimum wage. If tips fall short, employers are required to make up the difference, according to the Department of Labor and Regulation.

 Even with the increase, the average monthly cost for a family of four is estimated at $5,014/month . To cover this on a single 40-hour income, you would need a pre-tax wage of roughly $30.00+/hr, $75,000–$85,000 annually (about $36–$41/hr). A single person needs $60,000 a year or more than twice this new minimum wage.
